title: Which Archived Results Survive a Rule Change? A Case Study in Revalidating Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2611.26666v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A research workflow can retain a correct numerical result after the evidence or approval that supported its use has expired. Common incremental build methods identify reusable computations, while deciding what remains usable also requires knowing which policy justified each approval. We examined a recorded parser migration across 312 paired research records, replayed both parsers with the same inputs, applied a calculation-file omission to the complete cohort, and evaluated current proof in a GNU Make comparison. Treating the prior projections as current would change at least one field in 11 of 312 records, and controlled cases show that even matching values can lack a current proof. The study separates numerical recovery from applicable approval and sets out the conditions under which a maintained dependency graph can preserve both.

translated_title: 哪些存档结果能在规则变更后幸存？一项重新验证决策的案例研究
translated_abstract: 研究工作流可能在支持其使用的证据或批准已经过期之后，仍然保留正确的数值结果。常见的增量构建方法能够识别可重用的计算，而判断哪些内容仍然可用，还需要了解是哪项政策为每次批准提供了依据。我们检查了一次记录在案的解析器迁移，涉及312条成对研究记录，用相同的输入重放了两个解析器，对整个队列应用了计算文件遗漏处理，并在GNU Make比较中评估了当前的证明。将先前的投影结果视为当前结果，会导致312条记录中有11条的至少一个字段发生变化，且受控案例表明，即使数值完全匹配，也可能缺乏当前的证明。该研究将数值恢复与适用的批准区分开来，并阐明了在何种条件下，一个持续维护的依赖图能够同时保留这两者。
tldr: 该研究通过对312条成对记录的解析器迁移案例分析发现，数值结果的正确性与支持它的批准有效性是相互分离的——即使数值匹配，若相关政策已过期，结果也可能失去当前效力——并阐明了持续维护的依赖图在何种条件下能同时保留两者。
en_tdlr: Through a parser migration case study across 312 paired records, this study shows that numerical correctness and the validity of its supporting approval are distinct—even matching values can lack current proof—and sets out the conditions under which a maintained dependency graph can preserve both.
